title: Sport & Fair Play
description: From your course: talking about sport, winning and losing, fair play and cheating.

items.definition: the person or team that most people expect to lose
items.example: We went into the match as the [underdogs] and still won 3–1!
items.exampleRu: Нас считали аутсайдерами, а мы всё равно выиграли 3:1!
items.pattern: be the underdog(s); go into sth as the underdog(s)
items.trap: In sport, Russian «аутсайдер» is usually 'underdog', because an 'outsider' is mainly someone who doesn't belong to a group.

items.definition: the person or team that most people expect to win
items.example: I reckon Spain are [the favourites] to win the next World Cup.
items.exampleRu: По-моему, главный фаворит следующего чемпионата мира — сборная Испании.
items.trap: Say 'the favourites to win', not 'for winning', and in British English a team takes a plural verb: 'Spain are'.

items.definition: to make someone fall by putting your foot in their way
items.example: Someone [tripped me up] at five-a-side last night, and I twisted my ankle.
items.exampleRu: Вчера на мини-футболе мне кто-то поставил подножку, и я подвернул ногу.
collocations: the last question tripped me up
items.trap: The pronoun goes in the middle ('tripped me up', not 'tripped up me'), and it can also mean 'catch sb out with a tricky question'.

items.definition: to fall over on purpose in football so the referee thinks you were fouled
items.example: I can't stand players who [dive] every time someone comes near them.
items.exampleRu: Терпеть не могу игроков, которые падают, стоит кому-то к ним приблизиться.
items.trap: The rules call it 'simulation', but fans and commentators say a player 'dived' (the British past form).

items.definition: a free shot at goal after a foul near the goal; also a punishment such as a fine
items.example: After a 2–2 draw we lost on [penalties], which was absolutely gutting.
items.exampleRu: Сыграли 2:2 и проиграли по пенальти — было ужасно обидно.
items.pattern: take/score/miss a penalty; win/lose on penalties
items.trap: Russian «штрафной удар» is a 'free kick'; a 'penalty' is the kick from the spot, and 'on penalties' is always plural.

items.definition: to delay something on purpose to get more time
items.example: I said ‘good question’ just to [play for time] while I thought of an answer.
items.exampleRu: Я сказал «хороший вопрос», только чтобы потянуть время и придумать ответ.
items.trap: Not 'pull time' or 'stretch time' (calques of «тянуть время»); 'buy time' and 'stall for time' are close.

items.definition: to behave in a silly way instead of doing something useful
items.example: Stop [messing around] and help me pack the car — we're already late!
items.exampleRu: Хватит дурачиться, помоги загрузить машину — мы и так опаздываем!
items.pattern: mess around / mess around with sth
items.trap: Don't confuse it with 'mess sth up' (испортить, напортачить); 'mess about' means the same and is very British.

items.translation: отвлекать, сбивать с настроя; отбивать охоту
items.definition: to distract someone so they can't concentrate or do something well
items.example: Please don't talk while I'm serving — it really [puts me off].
items.exampleRu: Пожалуйста, не разговаривай, когда я подаю, — меня это очень сбивает.
items.trap: Not the same as 'put sth off' (откладывать), and the pronoun goes in the middle: 'it puts me off', not 'it puts off me'.

items.definition: to break a rule a little, usually to help someone
items.example: The receptionist [bent the rules] and let me into the gym without my card.
items.exampleRu: На ресепшене пошли мне навстречу и в обход правил пустили в зал без карты.
items.trap: 'Bend' is softer than 'break' (you break a rule a little, often to be kind), and the past form is 'bent', not 'bended'.

items.definition: not having lost a single game or match
items.example: Believe it or not, our Sunday league team is still [unbeaten] this season.
items.exampleRu: Хотите верьте, хотите нет, но наша любительская команда в этом сезоне ещё ни разу не проиграла.
items.pattern: be unbeaten (in ten games); an unbeaten run
items.trap: 'Unbeaten' means it hasn't lost yet, while 'unbeatable' means impossible to beat.

items.definition: to let the other team score; also to admit that you have lost or are wrong
items.example: We were 2–0 up and then [conceded] three goals in the last ten minutes.
items.exampleRu: Мы вели 2:0, а потом за последние десять минут пропустили три гола.
items.pattern: concede a goal / defeat; concede that ...
items.trap: Not 'miss a goal' (a calque of «пропустить гол»): if you miss, you fail to score yourself.

items.definition: to follow the rules and treat others honestly
items.example: Come on, [play fair] — you can't look at my cards!
items.exampleRu: Ну давай по-честному — нельзя подглядывать в мои карты!
items.trap: Say 'play fair', not 'play honest'; «фэйр-плей» is the noun 'fair play'.

items.definition: to do things in the honest, accepted way
items.example: I always [play by the rules] at work, even when others take shortcuts.
items.exampleRu: На работе я всегда играю по правилам, даже когда другие ищут обходные пути.
items.trap: Use 'by', not 'on' or 'with' (calques of «по правилам»).

items.definition: to get something that puts you in a better position than others
items.example: Speaking a second language can help you [gain an advantage] in the job market.
items.exampleRu: Знание второго языка может дать вам преимущество на рынке труда.
items.pattern: gain an advantage over sb / in sth
items.trap: Don't confuse it with 'take advantage of sth' (воспользоваться); we don't say 'receive an advantage'.

items.definition: to hit the ball in tennis, golf, cricket and similar sports
items.example: I tried to [play a shot] I'd seen on YouTube and almost hit my doubles partner.
items.exampleRu: Я попробовал повторить удар, который видел на YouTube, и чуть не попал в своего партнёра по паре.
items.trap: In tennis, golf and cricket you 'play' or 'hit' a shot, not 'do a hit' or 'make a strike'; in football you 'take a shot'.

items.definition: to make a game less enjoyable for everyone
items.example: One guy kept arguing with the ref and [spoilt the game] for everyone.
items.exampleRu: Один парень всё время спорил с судьёй и испортил игру всем.
items.trap: For fun and games use 'spoil' or 'ruin', not 'damage' or 'break' (calques of «испортить»); British English often uses the past form 'spoilt'.

items.definition: an event where people or teams compete in a sport
items.example: Every summer my company runs a [sports competition], and this year I'm doing the relay.
items.exampleRu: Каждое лето наша компания проводит спортивные соревнования, и в этом году я бегу эстафету.
items.pattern: enter / take part in a sports competition
items.trap: Use 'sports' with an -s before the noun, not 'sportive', and Russian plural «соревнования» is often a single 'competition'.

items.definition: to win against someone in a game or fight; also the act of losing
items.example: Last weekend our local team [defeated] the league leaders 3–1.
items.exampleRu: В прошлые выходные наша местная команда обыграла лидеров лиги со счётом 3:1.
items.trap: You 'defeat' or 'beat' a team but 'win' a game or a cup, so never 'we won them'.

items.definition: not equal or fair; also not flat or smooth
items.example: It was a really [uneven] contest — they were all twenty and we were over forty.
items.exampleRu: Силы были явно неравные: им всем по двадцать, а нам за сорок.
items.trap: It means both «неравный» and «неровный» (uneven ground), but «нечётное число» is an 'odd number', not an 'uneven' one.

items.definition: very angry and shocked about something, or feeling that it is very unpleasant
items.example: I was absolutely [disgusted] by how the fans treated the referee.
items.exampleRu: Меня до глубины души возмутило, как болельщики обращались с судьёй.
items.trap: 'Disgusted' is how you feel and 'disgusting' is what causes it; both are much stronger than 'annoyed'.

items.definition: to pretend that you are hurt
items.example: At school I once [faked an injury] to get out of cross-country.
items.exampleRu: В школе я однажды симулировал травму, чтобы не бежать кросс.
items.trap: Not 'imitate an injury' (imitate = copy sb) or 'fake a trauma', because 'trauma' in English usually means a deep emotional shock.

items.definition: to be ordered by the referee to leave the field for breaking the rules
items.example: My first ever match ended early: I [got sent off] for swearing at the ref.
items.exampleRu: Мой самый первый матч быстро закончился: меня удалили за то, что я выругался на судью.
items.pattern: get sent off (for sth / for doing sth)
items.trap: Not 'got deleted' (a calque of «удалили»), and spell it 'off', not 'of'; American English says 'get ejected'.

items.definition: so bad that it makes people angry or ashamed
items.example: Waiting three weeks for a refund is [disgraceful] — I'm writing a complaint.
items.exampleRu: Три недели ждать возврата денег — это возмутительно, я пишу жалобу.
items.trap: 'Disgraceful' describes a thing or behaviour; 'disgraced' describes a person who has lost respect, and 'disgusted' is how you feel.

items.definition: to break the rules to win or get something
items.example: My sister always [cheats] at Monopoly, so nobody wants to play with her.
items.exampleRu: Моя сестра вечно жульничает, когда играет в «Монополию», поэтому с ней никто не хочет играть.
items.pattern: cheat at cards / in an exam / on sb
items.trap: You cheat 'at' a game and 'in' an exam, but 'cheat on sb' means «изменять» a partner.

items.translation: выйти сухим из воды, остаться безнаказанным
items.definition: to do something wrong and not be caught or punished
items.example: I parked there for three hours without paying and somehow [got away with it].
items.exampleRu: Я простоял там три часа, не заплатив за парковку, и мне это каким-то чудом сошло с рук.
collocations: let sb get away with sth
items.pattern: get away with sth / with doing sth
items.trap: 'Get away with sth' means «сойти с рук», while 'get away from sth' means escape or leave a place.

items.definition: always wanting to win and be better than other people
items.example: I get really [competitive] at pub quizzes, even though I pretend I don't care.
items.exampleRu: На квизах в пабе я становлюсь страшно азартным, хотя делаю вид, что мне всё равно.
items.trap: About a person it means «любящий соревноваться», but about prices or a market it means «конкурентоспособный».

items.definition: to win or be the most successful in the end
items.example: Five of us applied for the same promotion, and I [came out on top].
items.exampleRu: На одно повышение претендовали пятеро, и победа осталась за мной.
items.trap: No article: 'on top', not 'on the top', which means on the upper surface of something.

items.definition: to lose on purpose so that the other person wins
items.example: I used to [let my nephew win] at chess, but now he actually beats me.
items.exampleRu: Раньше я поддавался племяннику в шахматах, а теперь он и правда меня обыгрывает.
items.trap: No 'to' after 'let': 'let him win', not 'let him to win' or 'give him to win' (a calque of «дать выиграть»).

items.definition: to be ready to do anything, even something unfair, to win
items.example: Playing tennis with my boss is stressful because he has to [win at all costs].
items.exampleRu: Играть в теннис с начальником — сплошной стресс: ему нужно победить любой ценой.
items.pattern: win at all costs; a win-at-all-costs mentality
items.trap: Use 'at' and plural 'costs', not 'by any price' or 'for any price' (calques of «любой ценой»).

items.definition: to feel proud and not ashamed, even after losing or failing
items.example: We lost the final, but we played fair, so we can [hold our heads up high].
items.exampleRu: Мы проиграли финал, но играли честно, так что нам нечего стыдиться.
items.trap: Change 'your' to match the subject (we → our heads), and don't confuse it with 'keep your chin up' (не вешай нос).

items.definition: a group of friends who play together in a quiz, often in a pub
items.example: Our [quiz team] meets at the pub every Thursday, and we've still never won.
items.exampleRu: Наша команда по квизам каждый четверг собирается в пабе, и мы до сих пор ни разу не выиграли.
items.pattern: be in a quiz team (UK) / on a quiz team (US)
items.trap: «Команда» here is 'team', never 'command', and in British English you are 'in' a team (US: 'on').
